target_customer: Hospitals and ICUs, and pharma partners running CAR-T programs (original); public health and testing programs (2020 COVID pivot)
problem: Critically ill patients' immune response (cytokines) could not be monitored rapidly at the bedside to tailor treatment; in 2020 the same sensor was aimed at a rapid saliva SARS-CoV-2 antigen test.
business_model: Diagnostic device and consumable sensor sales plus pharma partnerships (stated on YC page); no pricing sourced

founders.background_notes: 2017 U-M Graduate Student Entrepreneur of the Year per YC bio.

founders.background_notes: Described as a U-M physician in a 2016 Concentrate article; no further bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a novel nanosensor platform spun out of a university lab, FDA Breakthrough Device pathway work and semiconductor-style manufacturing, which is hardware and regulatory heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Patent-pending technology licensed from a U-M lab (2016 article) and an FDA Breakthrough Device designation; no sourced evidence on actual patent grants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the wedge.

market_need_then: Evidence is thin: a 2016 article says the goal was to bring precision care to ICU patients, and the YC page says pharma partners wanted to monitor immune response after CAR-T. No spend or regulation data was sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: No source covers brand; only a trademark filing (PREDXION) that was abandoned for no statement of use, notice dated 2022-12-12 per a search snippet.

pivots.from: Rapid cytokine and biomarker monitoring for critically ill patients (CAR-T, CRS)
pivots.why: COVID-19 pandemic need for scalable rapid testing, per the YC description; the company's own reasons not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Directory status is Inactive, but no shutdown announcement, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause of the stop is not public. Visible facts: a University of Michigan spinout founded around 2016-17, YC S17, FDA Breakthrough Device designation, pharma partnerships for CAR-T monitoring, and a 2020 pivot toward a saliva COVID antigen test, with funding amounts conflicting and unverified. A trademark abandoned in December 2022 suggests activity had ended by then, which is an inference not a sourced reason.
notes: Unverified funding: Seedtable lists a $120K seed in 2017-08; Dealroom and a startup map list about $6.3M total with no investors; neither is a primary source so no round is recorded.
